passage:
Counsellor's note, Thursday. Gurleen writing about Zainab.
Zainab first came to me fourteen months ago, to think about moving abroad. Since then Zainab has read forum threads, kept four spreadsheets and updated them after every new post. Every session opens with a new comparison. Two application windows have closed. Each time Zainab said, "There's more I should look at first."
Zainab looked tired, and said, "What if I choose wrong?" Choosing nothing, I said gently, is also a choice, and it is being made anyway. I asked Zainab to set a date for a decision and to name the single fact still missing.
Zainab stayed quiet, then wrote the date in the diary.
— Gurleen

qa.a: Zainab is afraid of making the wrong choice, which keeps the research going and the decision on hold.

qa.a: Zainab could set a decision date, name the one missing fact and stop researching once that is answered.

qa.q: What is it like for Gurleen to watch Zainab's research go on?
qa.a: Gurleen feels concerned and patient, noting the delay and choosing to say gently that not choosing is also a choice.

grounding: The note shows a person comparing countries for over a year with forums and spreadsheets until application windows close and the delay becomes the decision.

passage:
31 January
The Germany master's deadline closed today. I knew it would. I watched the date come closer on my spreadsheet for three weeks and kept adding columns instead of filling the form.
Kishore called at night. He asked, gently, 'So which country did you pick in the end?' I didn't have an answer. A year of forums, fourteen tabs, a spreadsheet with forty rows comparing rent, weather, part-time job rules, even how many Indian grocery shops each city has. And I haven't applied to a single place. Canada's intake closed in November while I was reading about housing in the Netherlands.
Tonight it hit me that not choosing was a choice. I chose staying, without ever deciding to.
Leela

qa.q: How many rows does Leela's spreadsheet have?
How does Leela feel when it hits that not choosing was a choice?
qa.a: Leela feels regretful and frustrated, seeing that a year of research ended with no application at all.

qa.q: What could Leela try differently for the next intake?
qa.a: Leela could set a firm cut-off for research, pick the top two options by then and apply, since a good-enough choice beats a perfect one never made.

qa.q: How might Kishore feel after asking his gentle question?
qa.a: Kishore may feel sad for Leela and careful not to add pressure, sensing that the question stung.

grounding: It shows someone comparing countries for a year on forums and spreadsheets until application windows close and the delay decides for them.

Dilnaz: did you apply to the Australia one? deadline was yesterday
Ramesh: not yet. was comparing Perth vs Adelaide rent again
Dilnaz: Ramesh you said that in March
Ramesh: I know. but I found a new forum thread about job markets, it changes things
Dilnaz: it's September.
Ramesh: I just want to be sure 😕
Dilnaz: you've made three spreadsheets. how many forms have you filled
Ramesh: ...zero
Dilnaz: the NZ window closed in July. Canada in May. now this
Ramesh: so I missed all of them?
Dilnaz: you didn't miss them. you let them go by
Ramesh: that hurts
Dilnaz: I'm not trying to hurt you. pick ONE for the next round and I'll sit with you while you fill it

What was Ramesh feeling on typing 'that hurts'?
qa.a: Ramesh felt stung and ashamed, seeing that every window had closed during all that comparing.

qa.q: Which approach would suit Ramesh better next round?
qa.a: Picking one option with a fixed date to apply, as Dilnaz offers, and accepting that no forum thread will bring full certainty.

qa.q: How does Ramesh's delay look to Dilnaz?
qa.a: Dilnaz is frustrated after hearing the same thing since March, but still cares enough to offer to sit alongside while the form gets filled.
